IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED as Gerrit change 2643 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2643 — awaiting LLM-Review and Verified. NOT closed, NOT submitted; ticket deliberately left in_progress.

PLAN REVIEW PASSED ON THE FIRST PASS, certified at verified_at_sha 446b1ba27770, no blocking and no advisory findings — three coaching moves only. Two of them are answered by this comment (attestation evidence recorded on the ticket; per-AC worked examples named below). The third was substantive and changed the code, see "the riskiest assumption" below.

## What actually enforces the bound, and how strongly

`SystemMaxUse=` is a REAL cap enforced by the writer: journald checks it SYNCHRONOUSLY as it extends a journal file and vacuums to stay under it. That is materially stronger than S2's image/layer share, which has no ceiling at all and is held only by retention. Two residuals are written into the script, the alarm text and the runbook rather than glossed:
 - only ARCHIVED files are vacuumed, so real usage can exceed the ceiling by up to one active file (`SystemMaxFileSize`, default 1/8 of it) — the honest worst case is 9/8 x cap, i.e. 3.375 GiB at the 3 GiB default, not 3 GiB;
 - it bounds `/var/log/journal` ONLY, not the rest of `/var/log` (~0.1G of the 1.8G at the incident), which stays on the root-disk backstop.

AND — the trap this story could have walked into — journald is ALREADY capped. `SystemMaxUse` defaults to 10% of the filesystem capped at 4G, which resolves to 4 GiB on this 60 GiB root, and the journal measured 1.7G, i.e. it was INSIDE its implicit ceiling at the outage. "Bound an unbounded journal" would have been false. What the explicit 3 GiB buys is stated in the tree: a smaller ceiling that does NOT move when the volume is resized, a ceiling readable on the box instead of only inside journald, and a named generator.

Two knobs the ticket named were DECLINED with reasons rather than set. `SystemKeepFree=` defaults to 15% capped at 4G and is therefore already AT its cap here — pinning it changes nothing and pinning a smaller value would WEAKEN the free-space floor. `RuntimeMaxUse=` governs `/run/log/journal`, which is tmpfs: RAM, not the root volume, and so belongs to the memory budget ADR 0079/0104 own.

## The S2 lesson applied: activation is OBSERVED, never inferred

journald reads its config at STARTUP and `systemd-journald.service` implements NO `ExecReload`, so `systemctl reload` cannot apply this and its zero exit would prove nothing — exactly the false evidence S2 removed when it deleted `systemctl reload docker`. So `--install` restarts the logger ONLY when the drop-in changed, and then decides activation INDEPENDENTLY from the kernel: `/proc/<MainPID>`'s mtime against the drop-in's mtime, failing closed on an unreadable PID, an unreadable mtime, an absent drop-in, or a daemon that predates the file.

`test_a_successful_restart_is_not_itself_reported_as_activation` is the pin: `systemctl restart` exits 0 and the script still reports NOT in effect, because the fake `/proc` entry predates the write. `test_a_reload_is_never_used_as_evidence_that_the_ceiling_took` pins that no `reload` is issued at all.

## The coaching move that changed the code: the riskiest assumption, PROBED

The plan asserted that restarting journald is safe where restarting Docker was not. The reviewer's coaching was to test that assumption first, and it was right to single it out — if it did not hold, the restart would sever the stdout log streams of already-running services, which would in turn quietly ZERO the marker-count metrics observability.sh derives from those journals (VOTER_ERROR, AUTODEPLOY_*, ...): healthy-looking readings from a box that stopped reporting.

Verified against the shipped unit rather than asserted: `units/systemd-journald.service.in` carries `Sockets=systemd-journald.socket systemd-journald-dev-log.socket` (PID 1 owns the listening sockets) and `FileDescriptorStoreMax=4224` plus `FileDescriptorStorePreserve=yes`, whose upstream comment is literally "Ensure services using StandardOutput=journal do not break when journald is stopped". So the mechanism is real.

It is nonetheless CHECKED rather than believed: `restart_journald` probes `FileDescriptorStoreMax` on the live unit and REFUSES the restart when the store is absent or unreadable, leaving the ceiling dormant and saying so. A dormant ceiling is a capacity problem the alarms announce; a severed log stream is a blind spot that looks like health. `test_the_restart_is_refused_when_journald_has_no_file_descriptor_store` pins it, and was proven non-vacuous: deleting the guard makes it fail with `assert 'restart' not in '...'`.

## Both sides of the ratio span the same bytes (S2's third trap, in ratio form)

`SystemMaxUse` governs the journal files under `/var/log/journal`, so the numerator is a bounded `du -sx --block-size=1` of exactly that tree — never `/var/log`, which the ceiling does not bound and which would make the percentage a ratio about no quantity at all. `test_the_percent_is_measured_over_the_tree_the_ceiling_governs` reads back every path `du` was actually asked about and asserts the journal tree is among them and `/var/log` is not. The one residual runs the safe way and is documented: `du` counts every byte in the tree while journald's quota counts only its own `*.journal*` files, so a stray file OVER-reports and pages early rather than reading healthy.

## The heartbeat closes a gap S2's own AC review named

S2's AC verification recorded that its BuildKit share "stays UNCAPPED on this box until an operator schedules a restart... the runbook documents the step; nothing tracks that it happened." `journal_cap_in_effect` tracks it: a 1/0 heartbeat on EVERY tick including the 0 path (the bug bff5 rule), asserting continuously that the ceiling the percentage is measured against is the one the running daemon actually read. Without it, a dormant ceiling makes `journal_used_percent` a ratio against a denominator that is not in force — and every other reading looks healthy.

## Two alarms, because neither implies the other

`rebar-journal-usage-high` (`journal_used_percent` > 85, Maximum) and `rebar-journal-cap-not-in-effect` (`journal_cap_in_effect` < 1, Minimum — the `rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted` shape). Both 300/3/2, both dimensionless on both sides, both `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, both SNS-wired on `alarm_actions` AND `ok_actions`, both pinned BY RESOURCE LABEL in `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` with the anti-vacuity floors raised 21 -> 26 total (24 -> 26) and 19 -> 21 host.

## RED evidence

test_journald_cap.py: 15 failed / 0 passed before `journald-cap.sh` existed. test_observability_journal.py: 8 failed / 1 passed before §2g — and the 1 pass was the vacuous negative (`publishes nothing` is trivially true when the metric does not exist), correctly identified as vacuous rather than counted as coverage. The fd-store guard was separately proven non-vacuous by deleting it and watching its test fail.

## Verification (deliberately NOT `make verify` — see below)

make lint 0 (complexity active=33 new=0 increased=0 stale=16; mechanism active=684 new=0 increased=0 — no `mechanism-ok` marker needed, the detectors scan src/ and scripts/, not infra/; shellcheck, deploy-manifest, zizmor and actionlint all clean). make typecheck 0 (762 files). `terraform fmt -check -recursive` 0; `init -backend=false` + `validate` Success. NO TERRAFORM WAS APPLIED.

Tests, all green: the two new files (27) + test_docker_storage_cap.py + test_observability_docker_storage.py + test_alarm_actions_terraform.py (74 together) + the remaining eleven observability suites and the terraform/infra guards (49 + 162). The three pytest-only gates — test_mechanism_delta, test_api_surface_gate, test_predates_gate_guard_parity — 56 passed after `git add`.

`make verify` was NOT run, at the operator's explicit instruction: the Gerrit host went fully offline for 41 minutes tonight from root-volume EBS IOPS saturation, very likely caused by concurrent agents running plan-review gates and full local suites. A broader blast-radius selection WAS started and then deliberately stopped when the host's load average was measured at 53 with another worktree's full suite running; the selections above stand in for it, and CI's Verified +1 is the authoritative full-suite result. `scripts/check_orphaned_load.py` is clean and my pytest processes were confirmed reaped (the survivors belong to another worktree).

## Discovered work, filed rather than folded in

octahedral-auburn-sunfish (5246-2ec0-1fa6-4637), linked discovered_from: NEITHER `docker-storage-cap.sh` NOR `journald-cap.sh` is listed in any of autodeploy.sh's `*_PATHS` manifests. Their CONSUMERS are (observability.sh via OBS_PATHS, compose-up.sh via MATERIALIZER_PATHS), but a commit that changes only a cap value — the exact edit ADR 0112 decision 6 says an operator should be able to make — signals nothing. `check_deploy_manifest.py` does not catch it because it derives from Dockerfile/compose references and from `materialize-*.sh` / `*-entrypoint.sh` / `compose-up.sh` filename conventions, and `*-cap.sh` matches none. It was NOT fixed here because `autodeploy.sh` is outside this story's declared file_impact and adding it would invalidate a signed attestation whose currency basis IS the file impact — and because the gap is shared with S2, so it is one change there rather than half a change here.

## Notes for the sibling stories

S2's two carry-over notes still stand and I deliberately did not act on them: compose-up.sh now has SIX independent `if ! bash ...; then echo WARN; fi` blocks and S4/S5 will add more; observability.sh is now ~1120 lines and each story re-spells the put-metric-data + logger pair. The one shared thing I did extract is `docker_pct_of` -> `pct_of_cap` (a 3-line behaviour-preserving rename), since §2g needed the same clamp and a `docker_`-prefixed helper used for the journal would read wrong.

## File impact UNCHANGED since the certified review

Exactly the eight declared paths; no file added or dropped, so the signed plan-review attestation stands and no re-review was forced.

compiled_state.description:
# S3 — Bound journald storage and alarm on journal saturation

## Why
ADR 0112 decisions 1+2, the **journald** accumulator. At the 2026-09-02 outage the root
volume's 28G working set included `/var/log` at 1.8G, of which the **journal was 1.7G** (every
compose service logs to the host journal), and the only signal was `rebar-root-disk-pressure`
— "root disk high", which cannot name the accumulator.

## What bounds journald, and how strongly — stated before the design
`SystemMaxUse=` is a **real cap enforced by the writer**, checked **synchronously as journald
extends a journal file**; materially stronger than S2's image/layer share, which has no ceiling
at all. Two residuals, written into the tree rather than glossed:
1. **Only ARCHIVED files are vacuumed** — the ACTIVE file is never deleted, so usage may exceed
   the cap by one file, bounded by `SystemMaxFileSize` (default 1/8 of `SystemMaxUse`): worst
   case 9/8 × cap = **3.375 GiB for the 3 GiB cap**, not 3 GiB.
2. **It bounds `/var/log/journal`, not `/var/log`** — the remainder (~0.1G of the 1.8G) stays
   covered only by the root-disk backstop.

And the trap: **journald is ALREADY capped.** `SystemMaxUse=` defaults to 10% of the filesystem
capped at 4G — 4 GiB here — and the journal measured 1.7G, i.e. *inside* its implicit ceiling,
so "bound an unbounded journal" would be false. What this buys: an **explicit, smaller (3 GiB)
ceiling pinned regardless of volume size**, **readable on the box** rather than only inside
journald's head, and a **named generator** — the gap decision 2 exists to close.

## Design
### 1. `infra/scripts/journald-cap.sh` (new) — single source of truth
Mirrors S2's `docker-storage-cap.sh`.
- `--print-env` (`JOURNAL_MAX_USE_BYTES`, `JOURNAL_DIR`, `JOURNALD_DROPIN`) — side-effect-free,
  `eval`-consumed by `observability.sh`, so the published percent-of-cap and the cap journald is
  told to enforce are **the same number by construction**.
- `--print-conf` renders to stdout and writes nothing (the `--print-json` precedent), so it is
  testable with no root and no systemd; `--check-active` prints `1`/`0`;
  `--install` renders, no-ops if unchanged, else writes, restarts, then OBSERVES.

Measured env-settable default (decision 6): **3 GiB** — 1.76× the measured 1.7G, 25% below the
derived 4 GiB, volume-size independent. Drop-in
`/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/99-rebar-disk-ceiling.conf`: the `99-` prefix is load-bearing,
since systemd merges drop-ins in lexicographic filename order and the last wins.

**Two knobs are DECLINED, not set because the ticket named them.** `SystemKeepFree=` is
already at its 4G default cap here, so pinning it changes nothing and pinning it *smaller*
would WEAKEN the free-space floor; `RuntimeMaxUse=` governs tmpfs — **RAM, not root**. No
`.bak` set is kept: this script owns the drop-in, so the undo is `rm` + restart.

### 2. Activation is OBSERVED, never inferred from an exit status (the S2 lesson)
journald reads its config **at startup** and `systemd-journald.service` implements **no
`ExecReload`**, so a `reload` cannot apply this — and a meaningless zero exit is the false
evidence S2 removed with `systemctl reload docker`. `--install` therefore **restarts**
`systemd-journald` only when the rendered drop-in differs from disk — safe where `restart
docker` was not: journald's sockets are PID-1-activated and its stdout stream fds live in the
service's fd store and are restored, so no service goes down or loses its log stream — and then
**observes** the outcome
independently: mtime of `/proc/<journald MainPID>` (set by the kernel at process creation) vs
the drop-in's mtime, `started >= written` meaning in force. Anything undeterminable **fails
closed** as NOT in effect; the restart's exit status is never read as activation.

### 3. `observability.sh` §2g — both sides span the same bytes
S2's differencing lesson generalises to a ratio: numerator and denominator must cover the same
byte set. The denominator is `SystemMaxUse`, applied to the journal files under
`/var/log/journal`, so the numerator is a bounded `du -sx --block-size=1` of exactly that tree.
Residual: `du` counts every byte there, journald's quota only `*.journal*`, so stray files
**over**-report — the safe direction.
- `journal_bytes` (Bytes) and `journal_used_percent` (Percent, clamped to 100 like §2f) —
  published ONLY on a successful measurement, so an unmeasurable probe publishes NOTHING,
  `breaching` pages on the silence; a fabricated 0 would read as an empty journal.
- `journal_cap_in_effect` (1/0) — a **heartbeat on every tick**, including the 0 path, per
  `gate_scratch_mounted` (bug bff5). It closes a named gap: S2's AC review recorded that its
  BuildKit share "stays UNCAPPED… nothing tracks that it happened."

### 4. Two alarms (`monitoring_autodeploy.tf`), house 300/3/2 idiom
`rebar-journal-usage-high` (`journal_used_percent` > 85, `Maximum`) and
`rebar-journal-cap-not-in-effect` (`journal_cap_in_effect` < 1, `Minimum` — the
`rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted` shape). Neither implies the other (the 3e92 argument): a journal
under a cap that is **not in force** reads healthy on the first alarm. Both are dimensionless
on both sides, `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, SNS-wired on both action lists, and
**pinned by resource label** in
`tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`, floors raised 24 -> 26 and 19 -> 21. Terraform is
WRITTEN and VALIDATED only; `apply` is an operator step.

### 5. Install point + scope
One non-fatal `if ! bash …/journald-cap.sh --install; then echo WARN; fi` block in
`compose-up.sh` beside the `docker-storage-cap.sh` one. OUT of scope: the compose logging
driver, scratch placement (aa40), the Docker budget (9183), `/var/tmp` (S4), container layers
(S5), non-journal `/var/log`.

## Grounding
`infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh`; `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §2f (210-412), §2e
(164-209); `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:324`. `journald.conf(5)`: defaults are
"10%… and… 15% of the size of the respective file system, but each of the calculated default
values is capped to 4G"; "size limits are enforced synchronously when journal files are
extended"; "only archived files are deleted". `systemd-journald.service(8)`: no `ExecReload`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `--print-conf` renders a drop-in setting `SystemMaxUse=` from
      `JOURNAL_MAX_USE_BYTES`, writes nothing, and needs no root/systemd/journald.
- [ ] AC2 — `--install` is idempotent: a second run against an identical drop-in writes
      nothing and does NOT restart journald.
- [ ] AC3 — `--install` restarts `systemd-journald` only when the drop-in changed, and never
      reports "in effect" from that command's exit status; a test pins that no `systemctl
      reload` is used as evidence.
- [ ] AC4 — activation is decided by live journald start time vs the drop-in's mtime and FAILS
      CLOSED: an unreadable PID or mtime, or a daemon predating the file, reports NOT in
      effect.
- [ ] AC5 — `journal_bytes` and `journal_used_percent` are published only on a successful
      measurement (a failed `du` publishes neither, not 0); `journal_cap_in_effect` on EVERY
      tick including the 0 path.
- [ ] AC6 — `journal_used_percent` is computed against the same byte set the cap governs
      (`/var/log/journal` vs `SystemMaxUse`) and is clamped to 100.
- [ ] AC7 — Terraform declares both alarms with `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and SNS on
      both action lists, pinned by resource label with the floors raised; `fmt -check` and
      `validate` pass and nothing is applied.
- [ ] AC8 — the runbook documents the cap and its honest strength (archived-only overshoot, the
      `/var/log` remainder), both alarms, diagnosis, remediation (`journalctl --vacuum-size=`),
      and that a cap can be installed but not in force.
- [ ] AC9 — every new test runs offline over PATH stubs and a fake `/proc`: no systemd, no
      journald, no AWS, no CI provider (the portability criterion).

file_impact.reason: NEW: the single source of truth for the journald disk ceiling — renders and installs the journald.conf.d drop-in, prints the cap for observability.sh, and OBSERVES activation.
One non-fatal --install block beside the docker-storage-cap.sh one.
New section 2g: publish journal_bytes, journal_used_percent and the journal_cap_in_effect heartbeat.
Document the cap, its honest enforcement strength, both alarms, diagnosis and remediation.
NEW: cover the rendered drop-in, install idempotence, the restart-only-on-change rule, and fail-closed activation.
NEW: cover metric emission, publish-nothing-on-failed-measurement, the heartbeat, and the clamp.
Pin both new alarms by resource label in the breaching watched set and raise the anti-vacuity floors.
